metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: High-dimensional visual inputs (traffic video frames) from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, serving as the primary input for the DRL method. Three consecutive frames (4x512 pixels each after down-sampling) are stacked to represent the traffic state.
nodes_source.size_estimate: one observation is 4x512 in pixels. Three consecutive observations are stacked
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data. The simulation time is 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Figure 6 presents the 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic data, specifically 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp, used for calibrating simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors in SUMO.
nodes_source.size_estimate: 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas. The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
nodes_source.description: Data generated by removing information from specific subareas of the control area from the original traffic video data, used for perturbation analysis to evaluate the impact of missing information.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: derived from original data which is available upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations, form position matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are extracted from raw traffic video frames and then converted into position matrices to represent the traffic state.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, 0/2 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Position matrices are down-sampled to reduce input dimensions for computational efficiency while retaining vehicle position information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, 0/1 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Stack position matrices to form state
nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st: St = {mt-(N-1),..., mt}.
nodes_process.description: Down-sampled position matrices from N consecutive time steps are stacked to form the traffic state `st` for the DRL method.

nodes_process.node_name: Train Deep Q-network for ramp metering
nodes_process.source_quote: We propose a DRL method for local ramp metering based on traffic video data.
nodes_process.description: A Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) method is used to train a Q-network to approximate the optimal action-value function Q*(s,a) for local ramp metering. This involves using experience replay, a target network, and an e-greedy strategy. A multitask learning strategy is also implemented where the Q-network simultaneously predicts Q-value, mean speed, and queue length using a combined loss function (L1 for Q-value, L2 for speed/queue prediction). The Adam optimizer is used.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward rt after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward `rt` for the DRL agent is calculated based on the average speed `vt` in the merging area and the average queue length `qt` at the on-ramp, with weights `mu` and `omega`.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: The simulation environment is set up using SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator, to model the freeway network connecting Qingdao and Huangdao.

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is implemented as a baseline. It fixes the green phase length and determines the red phase length based on previous red phase length and downstream occupancies.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Simulation experiments are conducted for three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, DRL) to evaluate the proposed DRL method and compare it against baselines. Each scenario is run 20 times.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: Travel times in the mainline are evaluated and compared across the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios. Quartiles (Q1, Q2, Q3) and mean travel times are reported.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_process.description: The temporal-spatial distribution of mean speeds along the mainline is evaluated for the three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, DRL) to demonstrate efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: Queue lengths at the on-ramp are evaluated and compared across the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios, reporting quartiles and mean values.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_process.description: Traffic flows downstream of the merge area are evaluated and compared across the three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, DRL) to demonstrate DRL performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/1 tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is set up to evaluate the impact of video data information. The control area is divided into eight subareas, and information from each subarea is removed from the original data to create perturbed datasets.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate travel time with perturbed data
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: Travel times are evaluated using the perturbed datasets, with information removed from different subareas, and compared against a baseline using original data. Results are presented as box plots.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/3 tools named, no parameters stated.
